description: 2 tactical challenges for White in the Orthoschnapp Gambit. Play 4.Bd3! and trade into a better endgame.

drills.briefExplanation: 4.Bd3! Bxd3 5.Qxd3 e6 6.Nf3 — trade the bishops, centralize, develop.
drills.description: White to play. Black developed 3...Bf5 — challenge it with the Orthoschnapp 4.Bd3!.
drills.explanation: The Orthoschnapp Gambit: White meets the Caro-Kann Advance with 4.Bd3!, challenging Black's best piece. After 4...Bxd3 5.Qxd3 e6 6.Nf3 White has the bishop pair, a centralized queen, and a space advantage — Black's light-squared bishop, the soul of the Caro-Kann, is gone. A positional 'gambit' that wins the two bishops.
drills.name: The Bishop Challenge

drills.briefExplanation: 4.Bd3! Bxd3 5.Qxd3 e6 6.Nf3 — trade, centralize the queen, and develop.
drills.description: White to play. Play 4.Bd3! and follow up after the trade.
drills.explanation: The full Orthoschnapp sequence: 4.Bd3! Bxd3 5.Qxd3, and after 5...e6 White develops with 6.Nf3 — the queen is perfectly centralized, the bishop pair is secured, and Black's Caro-Kann has lost its best minor piece. White's space advantage (e5) plus the bishops is a lasting edge.
drills.name: Securing the Bishops
